steps.shell: for t in 0.28 0.31 0.34 0.37 0.40 0.44 0.48 0.52 0.56 0.60 0.64 0.68 0.72 0.76 0.80; do python3 qa/drive.py --port $PORT --display $DISPLAY set-prop time_of_day $t --path PixelDayNight >/dev/null; sleep 0.35; done

items.check: Close island, camera preview; the sky and light sweep dawn -> bright noon -> dusk -> night across the clip (not a far top-down view). No birds, no dust.
items.notes: The orbit clock does not advance in the editor, so time_of_day is stepped manually with set-prop during recording to drive the cycle. Camera distance is set to 55 BEFORE enabling preview (click 355,228); the orbit camera only re-reads distance when preview is (re)enabled.

items.check: Close island, dark/overcast stormy downpour with rain streaks and splashes; lightning bolts flash during the clip. Poster is the 5.6 s flash: a visible bolt and bright rainy sky.
items.notes: transition_seconds set to 0 so Storm applies in one frame. strike_lightning() fires bolts on demand. distance 55 set before enabling preview.

items.check: A clear spread flock of individual white pixel birds flying over the island (Animate on). Birds are big enough to read, not tiny dots.
items.notes: size 4 scales the birds up (camera-preview gives an active game camera); scare_distance 0 + landing off keep them in frame; separation up / cohesion down spreads the flock. distance 55 before preview.

items.check: Dark night island with glowing yellow/white fireflies blinking and wandering as clear specks over the island.
items.notes: time_of_day 0.93 (night) so night_only fireflies fade in; count/energy/size raised so they read. distance 55 before preview.

items.check: Close view of hex_island's ruin and pond with many pale one-pixel dust motes drifting over the grass (Beam 0, Density 1.0); birds and fireflies hidden so the motes are the only specks.
items.notes: Verified 2026-11-24 on :108/8908. The default field is deliberately faint (Density 0.2, Beam 1 = only inside god-ray shafts). Density 1.0 + Beam 0 makes the motes read, but only up close: at island distance a mote is a single pixel. hex_island opens already framed close on the ruin (the scene's own 3D camera), so no zoom steps are needed. Birds/Fireflies are hidden so their specks are not mistaken for dust.

items.check: A tall grey smoke plume rising from the island centre with a dark fire base, fully in frame, drifting with the wind. Plume is big and obvious.
items.notes: Adds a PixelSmoke via the Pixel World panel (Smoke & Fire + Add at 1259,528 with PixelSky selected, no scroll) and moves it onto the island centre (it spawns mid-air at the camera focus). Raise end_size so the plume reads at the far camera; crop top 168 keeps the plume tip in frame without the viewport toolbar. Node is session-only. Preview (355,228) is enabled so the viewport shows the scene Camera's close island view used by the media.

items.check: Fire spreading across the island's grass with orange flames and charring the ground, over the clip. Fire is big and obvious.
items.notes: Adds a PixelFireSystem under the terrain (Grass Fire + Add, panel scrolled down 8). ignite(pos, radius) must hit grass (ring positions, not the bare central mesa, which returns 0 cells). Record immediately after igniting so the active spread is captured. Node is session-only.

items.check: Night island (Time 0.95), close crop: a warm dithered lamp pool with a glowing core on the grass; the clip shows it flickering. 121 is the 2x still, 52 the clip + poster.
items.notes: Merged still+clip so the copy/paste rig setup runs once per session (the editor clipboard does not survive a session restart, so this must not be split across fresh_session items). Pixel World + Add creates a PixelLightVolume with no Light/Volume children, so the item copies the root of res://addons/MarchingSquaresTerrain/effects/pixel_light_volume.tscn and pastes it under WorldMood. Energy 20 / Pool Energy 2.5 / Pool Scale 1.5 / Radius 14, Flicker 0.6.
